objective: Add a deterministic 2-decimal summary line as the final line of every rendered payslip, and make compute_pay's deduction list deterministic by sorting it by name, so all compute_pay consumers (payslip and legacy export) are stable, with new tests for both changes and all existing tests kept passing.
in_scope: payroll/calc.py: compute_pay returns the deductions list sorted by name (insurance before tax); amounts, rates, and rounding unchanged

payroll/payslip.py: render_payslip appends a final line in the exact form 'Summary: net=<net> gross=<gross> deductions=<total>' with all three values formatted to 2 decimals and <total> the sum of all deduction amounts
New tests: exact-format summary line test in tests/test_payslip_summary.py (new file) and exact sorted-order test as a new method in the existing tests/test_payroll.py
New integration tests: contract-shape test tests/test_contract_shape.py (new) and E2E gate tests tests/test_payslip_integration.py (new)
Verification that payroll/legacy_export.py keeps passing with no code change and that its XML inherits the sorted deduction-element order with no other byte change

out_of_scope.reason: Marked LEGACY (HR-4411, removal scheduled Q3): docstring says do not extend or refactor, keep the byte format stable until cutover; its existing substring tests keep passing under the reorder.

out_of_scope.item: Adding a Summary line to the legacy XML export
out_of_scope.reason: The task defines the summary line as the final line of the payslip (render_payslip output); the XML format must stay byte-stable.

out_of_scope.item: Changing deduction rates (20% tax, 5% insurance), the gross/net formula, or rounding
out_of_scope.reason: The task changes order and presentation only; existing test test_compute_pay_values pins the values 8000.0/1600.0/400.0/6000.0.
Test fixture records e1/e2; the task does not ask for new employees or values.

out_of_scope.item: Refactoring or migrating the test suite (pytest, moving existing test methods, splitting files)
out_of_scope.reason: The repo uses unittest; moving existing tests is a refactor unrelated to the two requested changes.
Tracked by a separate ticket; the cutover is not part of this stage.

frozen_assumptions.statement: The deduction set stays exactly {tax: round(gross*0.20, 2), insurance: round(gross*0.05, 2)} as in calc.py today; only the order changes, never the amounts. Invalidated if the task is re-scoped to add, remove, or rename deductions.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: The task says make the existing list deterministic by sorting; existing tests pin all amounts.

frozen_assumptions.statement: The legacy_export 'keep the byte format stable until the cutover' requirement (HR-4411) means deterministic output across runs, not a frozen current insertion order: the task statement says sorting makes 'the payslip (and anything else built on compute_pay) stable', so the legacy XML deduction-element order becomes sorted (insurance before tax) and every other byte stays unchanged. Invalidated if the HR-4411 owner requires tax before insurance in the legacy XML.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: Both statements come from the same task text; the legacy test's substring assertions pass under the reorder either way.

frozen_assumptions.statement: The summary line is the last element of the list returned by render_payslip (appended after the 'Net: ...' line); render_payslip keeps returning list[str], not a joined string. Invalidated if a consumer requires a joined string or a different terminator.
frozen_assumptions.rationale: render_payslip currently returns list[str]; the task says the payslip 'must end with a final line', i.e. the last line of that artifact.

frozen_architecture.decision: The summary line is computed in payroll/payslip.py from the compute_pay result; payroll/calc.py stays a pure calculation returning {gross, deductions, net} with no formatting knowledge
frozen_architecture.rationale: Keeps the current module responsibilities: calc computes, payslip presents. Formatting in calc would leak presentation into the calculation layer.

frozen_architecture.decision: The legacy export path is unchanged structurally: legacy_export.py keeps reading compute_pay and rendering XML; only its deduction iteration order (inherited from compute_pay) changes
frozen_architecture.rationale: HR-4411 forbids extending or refactoring legacy_export; the sort belongs in compute_pay so every consumer inherits it.

shared_contracts.spec: payroll.calc.compute_pay(employee: dict with keys 'id','name','hourly','hours') -> dict with exactly the keys {'gross': float, 'deductions': list, 'net': float}; gross = round(hourly*hours, 2); deductions is a list of (name: str, amount: float) 2-tuples containing exactly ('tax', round(gross*0.20, 2)) and ('insurance', round(gross*0.05, 2)), sorted by name ascending (so 'insurance' precedes 'tax'); net = round(gross - sum(amounts), 2). Insertion order is no longer part of the contract.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: Only via a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST decided by the planning layer; executors may not edit the spec.

shared_contracts.spec: payroll.payslip.render_payslip(employee_id: str) -> list[str] with exactly the elements ['Payslip for {name} ({id})', '', 'Gross: {gross:.2f}', '  - {name}: {amount:.2f}' for each deduction in compute_pay order, 'Net: {net:.2f}', 'Summary: net={net:.2f} gross={gross:.2f} deductions={total:.2f}'], where total = sum of all deduction amounts and the summary line is the last element. For e1 the last element is exactly 'Summary: net=6000.00 gross=8000.00 deductions=2000.00'; for e2 'Summary: net=2700.00 gross=3600.00 deductions=900.00'.
shared_contracts.unfreeze_rule: Only via a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST decided by the planning layer; executors may not edit the spec.

integration_seams.description: payslip.py consumes the compute_pay result to render payslip lines including the new summary line; what can silently diverge: deduction-line order, the summary total, the 2-decimal formatting of the three values
legacy_export.py iterates compute_pay deductions to render the legacy XML; what can silently diverge: deduction-element order (byte stability vs deterministic sort per A-2), amount formatting

acceptance.description: render_payslip returns a payslip whose final line is the exact 2-decimal summary line
acceptance.positive_case: For e1: asserts lines[-1] == 'Summary: net=6000.00 gross=8000.00 deductions=2000.00' and lines[-2] == 'Net: 6000.00'; for e2: asserts lines[-1] == 'Summary: net=2700.00 gross=3600.00 deductions=900.00'
acceptance.negative_case: A payslip whose final line is missing, or is 'Summary: net=6000 gross=8000 deductions=2000' (no 2 decimals), fails the exact-equality test; the legacy XML contains no 'Summary' line
acceptance.failure_behavior: render_payslip('e999') raises KeyError from employees.get_employee exactly as before the change; no summary line is rendered
acceptance.evidence: tests/test_payslip_summary.py::test_summary_line_exact_format (assertEqual on lines[-1]) and tests/test_payslip_integration.py::test_e2e_payslip_full_text, both run via python -m unittest

acceptance.description: compute_pay returns the deductions list sorted by name
acceptance.negative_case: The old insertion order [('tax', 1600.0), ('insurance', 400.0)] fails the new test with an assertEqual mismatch
acceptance.failure_behavior: If the sort is removed, the new test fails with the insertion-order list; there is no silent fallback to insertion order

acceptance.description: All pre-change tests keep passing unmodified: the suite exits 0
acceptance.positive_case: The four pre-change test functions (test_compute_pay_values, test_deductions_covers_all_names, test_render_payslip_lines, test_export_shape) all report OK and the suite exits 0 with 0 errors
acceptance.negative_case: Any pre-change test erroring or failing fails this gate; existing test bodies must not be rewritten to make them pass
acceptance.failure_behavior: A non-zero exit code from python -m unittest discover blocks stage closure
acceptance.evidence: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' from the repo root → 'OK', exit code 0

acceptance.description: export_employee_xml returns byte-stable legacy XML with structure and values unchanged; only the deduction element order follows C1
acceptance.positive_case: asserts export_employee_xml('e1') contains '<gross>8000.00</gross>' and '<net>6000.00</net>', that '<deduction name="insurance">400.00</deduction>' precedes '<deduction name="tax">1600.00</deduction>', and that two consecutive calls return identical strings
acceptance.negative_case: The XML contains no new tags, no new attributes, no whitespace change, and no 'Summary' content
acceptance.failure_behavior: A byte difference between two consecutive calls fails the E2E gate (non-deterministic output)
acceptance.evidence: tests/test_payslip_integration.py::test_e2e_deterministic_renders (assertEqual on two calls) and ::test_e2e_legacy_export_order (ordered substring assertions)

acceptance.description: The contract-shape test verifies the final implementations match the frozen C1/C2 specs exactly
acceptance.positive_case: The shape test asserts compute_pay returns exactly the keys {gross, deductions, net}, deductions is a list of (str, float) 2-tuples sorted by name, and render_payslip's last element matches the regex '^Summary: net=\d+\.\d{2} gross=\d+\.\d{2} deductions=\d+\.\d{2}$'; all tests pass
acceptance.negative_case: An extra return key, a non-tuple deduction entry, an unsorted list, or a summary line without exactly 2 decimals fails a shape test
acceptance.failure_behavior: A shape test fails with the assertion diff; the integration task records the mismatch instead of patching the module

constraints.rule: No new runtime or test dependencies; stdlib + unittest only
Keep the existing unittest style and naming of tests/test_payroll.py; new test files follow the same style
Each task modifies only its owned_paths; payroll/legacy_export.py and payroll/employees.py are read-only for all tasks
No performance target beyond the existing pure-function implementation; sorting a 2-element list is trivial

resource_budget.stage_estimate: 2-4 h of agent time (two parallel leaves, then sequential integration gates)

open_questions.question: Does the HR-4411 'keep the byte format stable' requirement forbid reordering deduction elements in the legacy XML?
open_questions.resolution: Resolved by the task text itself: it explicitly says sorting makes 'the payslip (and anything else built on compute_pay) stable', so the reorder is in scope and all other bytes stay unchanged (assumption A-2). If the HR-4411 owner objects, raise request_contract_revision against C1.
